Tessera rover finds clay on Mars

By Staff Reporter

The Tessera rover has found clay minerals in an ancient crater on Mars, mission scientists said on Tuesday.

Clay forms in water, so the find suggests the crater once held a lake.

Lead scientist Priya Raman said the samples are about 3.5 billion years old.

The rover drilled 12 holes over six weeks to collect the material.

The team plans to drive north toward a second crater next month.
